_help: Hook lines for project mode (pipeline/projects.py expand): every planned storyboard video becomes a project of 4 versions (H1-H4) that differ only in the first 2-5 s: the spoken hook line, the opening shot and the label on screen. H1 is the planned hook; H2-H4 come from here, 4 DIFFERENT types per project, theme hooks first (make_batch.py THEMES), then the product's own lines, then the generic ones. Rules for every line: brand voice, short, spoken; only claims from docs/PLAYBOOK.md section 1 or the product's features; no fake testimonials ('I bought', 'my sister'), no invented numbers or superlatives ('10,000 women', 'best-selling'). Offer lines only through the placeholders make_batch.offer_vars() fills from the product's real offer ({P} '50%', {off_sp} 'fifty percent off', {price_sp} 'half price' at 50% else '<n> percent off', {gift_sp} 'a free matching pouch wallet', {GIFT_W} 'WALLET'; a [...] part drops out when its value is empty, a line whose value is empty outside [...] is skipped), and projects.py also drops any line or label new_product.unbacked() flags. Fields: text, type (one of 'types'), labels (2-4 words, uppercase, truthful; the first one not used yet in the project is shown), feature (a TAG of the product's features: the opening shot comes from that feature's picks when it can), formats (only for these storyboard formats: features / reviews / colours), per_feature (generic only: one line per product-file feature, {line} = its spoken line, {TAG} = its tag; a feature line may open a version even though the body says it later, never when block 1 says it). Product files have no entry under 'products': their own optional 'hooks' list (pipeline/data/products/README.md, checked by new_product.py check) comes first, then the per-feature and generic lines. Each line is at most 15 spoken words (projects.MAX_WORDS; colours videos add 'Which colour are you?'). Across a batch the least-used line is chosen first; a line repeated in another project gets another label (its own, then its type's) and another opening shot.

theme_hooks._help: make_batch.py THEMES hooks (template text as written there) -> type and labels. A theme hook missing here is typed by projects.classify() and gets its type's labels.
